purpose: Cilostazol is used to reduce leg pain and cramping that happens when you walk, a condition called intermittent claudication. It helps you walk farther and longer without that uncomfortable pain stopping you. It works by improving blood flow in the arteries of your legs.
how_it_works: Your blood vessels in your legs can become narrowed, making it hard for blood to flow through properly. Cilostazol works by relaxing and widening those blood vessels so more blood can get through. It also helps prevent blood platelets from sticking together and forming clots, which further improves circulation.
common_side_effects: Headache is the most common side effect and usually gets better over time. You may also notice a faster or pounding heartbeat, diarrhea, upset stomach, or dizziness. Some people experience soft stools or an abnormal stool consistency.
warnings: Important: This medication should NOT be used if you have heart failure of any kind — this is a serious safety concern. Tell your doctor about all your medications, especially blood thinners like warfarin or aspirin, as combining them increases bleeding risk. Avoid grapefruit juice, as it can raise the level of this drug in your blood. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 100 mg taken by mouth twice a day, about 30 minutes before or 2 hours after breakfast and dinner. Taking it with food can increase side effects, so it is best taken on an empty stomach. It may take 2 to 4 weeks before you notice improvement, and full benefit may take up to 12 weeks.
